description: A four-panel composite of EBSD phase maps (PM) overlaid on image-quality (IQ) maps of a low-density steel compressed along the compression axis (CA, marked by a double-headed arrow in the top-right of the upper panels) at (a) 500 and (b) 600 °C, 0.001 s⁻¹, true strain 0.6. Every panel carries a 20 µm scale bar. (a) and (b) are two-phase maps coloured by crystal structure: legend BCC = green, FCC = red, so that red FCC islands (austenite) lie within a dominant green BCC (ferrite) matrix; black/unindexed streaks and the grey IQ relief reveal deformation bands. (a) contains two white dashed boxes labelled (i) and (ii); (b) contains one box labelled (iii), marking regions selected for detail. (c) and (d) are the phase maps corresponding to (a) and (b) but resolve three constituent phases — Ferrite (green), Martensite (yellow), Austenite (red) — revealing a triplex microstructure. Banding is denser and more frequently distributed at 500 °C (a, c) than at 600 °C (b, d), where strain distribution is more homogeneous. Together the panels argue that warm deformation produces banded austenite in a ferrite matrix whose morphology and phase constitution depend on temperature.

observations.observation: Panels (a) and (b) are two-phase EBSD phase maps with legend BCC = green and FCC = red, showing red FCC (austenite) regions embedded in a dominant green BCC (ferrite) matrix.
Panels (c) and (d) use a three-phase legend: Ferrite = green, Martensite = yellow, Austenite = red.
Each of the four panels carries a 20 µm scale bar.
The compression axis (CA) is indicated by a double-headed arrow in the top-right corner of the upper panels.
White dashed boxes labelled (i) and (ii) are drawn in panel (a), and one box labelled (iii) in panel (b), marking detailed regions of interest.
Deformation bands are more frequently distributed through the microstructure under the lower compression temperature of 500 °C (Fig. 2a) and are not observed at 600 °C (Fig. 2b).
The corresponding phase maps (Fig. 2c and d) show a triplex microstructure after deformation to 0.6 strain.
The figure caption states the material was compressed at 500 and 600 °C under a strain rate of 0.001 s⁻¹ to a true strain of 0.6.
The strain localization at deformation bands seen in (a, c) is proposed to supply the driving force for simultaneous deformation-induced ferrite-to-austenite transformation.
The elongated red FCC/austenite islands in (a)-(d) are aligned roughly parallel to the indicated compression axis.
Yellow (martensite) regions in panels (c) and (d) are spatially associated with the banded features and with the red austenite areas.

subfigures.description: EBSD phase map on IQ map for the 500 °C condition, coloured BCC = green (matrix) with red FCC particles elongated along the compression axis; two white dashed boxes labelled (i) and (ii) outline regions of interest; 20 µm scale bar; CA arrow top right. Grey-black banded streaks mark deformation bands.

EBSD phase map on IQ map for the 600 °C condition, same BCC (green)/FCC (red) colouring; one white dashed box labelled (iii); 20 µm scale bar; CA arrow top right. Banding appears less frequent and more uniformly distributed than in (a).

Three-phase map corresponding to (a), legend Ferrite (green), Martensite (yellow), Austenite (red); yellow martensite bands accompany elongated red austenite within the green ferrite matrix; 20 µm scale bar.

Three-phase map corresponding to (b), same legend Ferrite (green), Martensite (yellow), Austenite (red); large interconnected yellow/orange banded regions with red austenite in a green ferrite matrix; 20 µm scale bar.
